title.text: The journey of a program: from text to execution

phrase.text: Before running a program, the engine breaks it into pieces, checks that it makes sense and translates it into simple instructions for its virtual machine.

runs.text: Before running a program, the engine breaks it into pieces, checks that it makes sense and translates it into simple instructions for its virtual machine.
When you press "Run", the program text travels along a path of five stages. Each stage produces something new from the previous one. Step through the figure to follow the program

runs.text: The text is split into pieces called tokens:
… Spaces and comments are kept aside.
The tokens are grouped into a tree: an algorithm containing a definition and a write.
The engine checks names and types:
The tree becomes an intermediate representation and then simple instructions for the virtual machine.
The virtual machine runs the instructions one by one and writes 42.
The first three stages form the

. If they find an error, the program does not run: it would make no sense to run something that is not understood. That is why a typing mistake shows up immediately, without waiting for the program to reach that line.

Some errors cannot be seen by the analysis because they depend on real values: dividing by zero, going outside an array or reading a variable without a value. Those are detected when running, at the exact moment they happen.

. Each line is a simple instruction;

points.text: The engine works in five stages: lexical, syntax, semantics, translation and execution.
If the analysis finds errors, the program does not run.
Errors that depend on concrete values appear when running.
